lines: +     * Whether the owner's tenure — the whole number of days from the registration date to the
+     * current server date — exceeds one year (strictly more than 365 days). This gates the top
+     * membership level: only an owner past a full year of tenure can reach level 4. A {@code null}
+     * registration date, or one in the future, counts as zero tenure and so never exceeds the
+     * threshold, which is why a newly created owner (zero tenure) can never exceed level 3.
+     * @param registrationDate the date the owner registered, or {@code null} when absent
+     * @return {@code true} when the tenure is strictly greater than 365 days

content.text:
The build is green — all 53 tests pass, including the new `Cp39Tests`.

## What I changed

The membership level was previously computed as `min(3, 1 + email + namesake0)`, hard-capping at 3 with no way to reach 4. I introduced tenure as the gate for level 4:

**`Owner.java`** — added a static helper:
```java
public static boolean tenureExceedsOneYear(LocalDate registrationDate)
```
It returns `true` only when the whole-day span from `registrationDate` to today is strictly greater than 365. A `null` or future registration date counts as zero tenure.

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — the `membershipLevel` expression now adds a `+1` tenure factor and raises the cap to 4:
```
min(4, 1 + email? + namesake0? + tenureOver365?)
```

Because a newly created owner is registered as of today (zero tenure), the tenure factor is 0, so the maximum a new owner can reach is `1 + 1(email) + 1(namesake0) = 3` — never 4, exactly as the spec requires. Only an owner past a full year of tenure can pick up the fourth point and reach level 4.
